key_insight: Varying oxygen pressure during BST thin-film growth produces ferroelectric, relaxor-like, or paraelectric behavior, linking deposition conditions to dielectric phase.
engineering_relevance: Oxygen growth pressure offers a fabrication control for engineering dielectric states in epitaxial BST devices relevant to future computing technologies.
method: Deposit SrRuO3/BST/SrRuO3 epitaxial heterostructures by pulsed laser deposition using a (Ba0.9Sr0.1)TiO3 target.
Systematically vary oxygen partial pressure during BST growth.
Map dielectric phase against growth pressure, film composition, and crystal structure; examine lattice changes using STEM.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three dielectric states across moderate pressure changes and STEM evidence of a tetragonal-to-nearly-cubic structural transition, with the nearly cubic lattice corresponding to relaxor-like behavior.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical pressure window, dielectric performance metrics, or reproducibility data to guide process transfer.
paper_title: Oxygen partial pressure induced dielectric phase evolution in PLD deposited Barium Strontium Titanate thin films
